yap-install.summary: Yap's .app bundle ships ONLY the Rust binary + icon — no Python, no venv, no mlx-whisper, no Whisper model (verified in target/release/bundle/macos/Yap.app: Contents/MacOS/wilson-voice + Resources/icon.icns; tauri.conf.json has no resources/externalBin). On a fresh Mac the runtime python resolver falls through to the /usr/bin/python3 Xcode-CLT shim, which exists as a file but cannot run anything, so ASR is structurally impossible while the app's own status logic reports python_ok=true ("Ready — hold fn⌃"). The guaranteed infinite-loading state on first run is the onboarding calibration step: the user records the phrase, taps stop, Onboarding sets busy=true and shows "Transcribing…", and the only thing that ever clears busy is a successful "transcript" event — the Rust error path emits no event Onboarding listens to, so on any ASR failure (certain on a fresh Mac) the overlay spins forever. Three more unbounded hangs compound it: "Install local ASR" is a synchronous Tauri command that runs `python -m venv` + `pip install mlx-whisper` on the MAIN thread with no timeout (whole app beachballs for minutes-to-forever); the one-shot ASR fallback uses Command::output() with no timeout while mlx_whisper downloads the ~1.6 GB whisper-large-v3-turbo model from HuggingFace inside the transcribe call, leaving busy=true ("Transcribing with local Whisper…") indefinitely; and the onboarding permissions step polls get_permissions every 1.2 s, each poll spawning the CLT python shim on the main thread (repeated "Install Command Line Developer Tools" dialogs). Onboarding never mentions the required ASR install at all — it only shows Microphone and Accessibility — so a fresh user has no path to a working install.

findings.title: App bundle contains no Python, no venv, no model, no ASR runtime — first run depends entirely on the host machine
findings.detail: The bundle config declares no resources and no externalBin/sidecar, so the built Yap.app contains only the Tauri binary and icon. asr_worker.py is embedded in the binary via include_str! and seeded to ~/Library/Application Support/WilsonVoice/asr_worker.py at launch, but the Python interpreter, the mlx-whisper package, and the Whisper model are all expected to be found/installed/downloaded on the user's machine at runtime. On a fresh MacBook Air (no Homebrew, no Xcode CLT, no prior venv) none of these exist. The venv is only created if the user finds and clicks 'Install local ASR' in the Permissions tab (requires network + a real system python3, which itself requires the multi-GB Xcode CLT install); the model (default mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo, ~1.6 GB) is only downloaded from HuggingFace by mlx_whisper on first preload/transcribe into ~/Library/Application Support/WilsonVoice/cache/huggingface/hub.
findings.evidence: tauri.conf.json:36-55 (bundle block: no resources, no externalBin); verified bundle listing: desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Yap.app/Contents/MacOS/wilson-voice + Contents/Resources/icon.icns only; asr_paths.rs:10 (include_str! of python/asr_worker.py), asr_paths.rs:19-36 (ensure_worker seeds to App Support); asr_paths.rs:82-131 (setup_local_venv: python -m venv + pip install mlx-whisper, user-triggered only); lib.rs:122 (default model whisper-large-v3-turbo); asr.rs:70-106 (HF cache env under App Support; network allowed only when snapshot absent)

findings.title: ROOT CAUSE of the infinite screen: onboarding calibration 'Transcribing…' can never resolve on a fresh Mac — busy is only cleared by a success event
findings.detail: First-run flow (settings.onboarded defaults false → Onboarding overlay renders full-screen). At the calibration step the user taps record, then taps stop; toggleCalibration sets busy=true and the button locks into disabled 'Transcribing…'. The ONLY code that resets busy is the listener for the 'transcript' event, which the backend emits solely on a successful pipeline. On the error path the backend only logs, sets last_error, and fires a macOS notification (which a fresh Mac may not even display since notification permission is unanswered) — it emits 'status' but Onboarding listens only to 'recording' and 'transcript'. On a fresh Mac ASR always fails (resolve_python returns /usr/bin/python3 — the CLT shim, or a CLT python without mlx_whisper: the warm daemon dies or returns ok:false ImportError, the one-shot fallback returns 'bad ASR JSON'), so the pipeline always errors and the overlay spins forever with zero surfaced error. This is the guaranteed, reproducible infinite-loading state on any machine without a working mlx venv.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:680-687 (onboarding gate); Onboarding.tsx:120-128 (toggleCalibration sets busy=true on stop), Onboarding.tsx:83-92 (only 'recording' and 'transcript' listeners; busy reset only inside the transcript handler), Onboarding.tsx:235-247 (disabled={busy}, label 'Transcribing…'); lib.rs:641-645 (Err path: log + last_error + notify only — no transcript/paste_outcome event); lib.rs:88-89 + lib.rs:137 (onboarded defaults false); asr_paths.rs:39-55 (fresh-Mac fallback to /usr/bin/python3); asr.rs:355-361 (warm fail → one-shot), asr.rs:411-416 ('bad ASR JSON' from empty shim output)

findings.title: 'Install local ASR' runs venv creation + pip install of mlx-whisper synchronously on the MAIN thread with no timeout — whole-app freeze/beachball, forever on stalled network
findings.detail: setup_asr_venv is a non-async Tauri command; the codebase's own comment on paste_entry documents that sync commands run ON the main thread. setup_local_venv runs Command::status() for `python -m venv` and `pip install -U pip mlx-whisper` (mlx + numpy + metal libs, hundreds of MB) with no timeout. While it runs, the entire NSApplication event loop is blocked: window beachballs, tray dead, all pending invokes queue — which the user experiences as an infinitely loading app. If pip's network stalls, it blocks permanently. On a CLT-less fresh Mac the bootstrap picks the /usr/bin/python3 shim (is_file() passes), `-m venv` fails fast, and the only surfaced feedback is a transient toast reading 'python -m venv failed'.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:960-963 (sync #[tauri::command] setup_asr_venv); lib.rs:871-877 (in-repo proof that sync commands run on main thread: 'a *sync* command runs ON main and would deadlock'); asr_paths.rs:98-124 (bootstrap candidate list including /usr/bin/python3; venv + pip via .status() with no timeout); App.tsx:798-810 (button handler; errors only via 2 s toast)

findings.title: First real transcribe triggers the ~1.6 GB model download under a 30 s timeout, then falls back to an UNTIMED one-shot — busy=true / 'Transcribing with local Whisper…' for the whole download or forever
findings.detail: The Whisper model is fetched lazily by mlx_whisper.load_model inside the transcribe/preload call. Preload (900 s leash) only runs at launch if the venv already exists, so on a fresh install the download instead happens during the user's FIRST dictation: the warm-daemon transcribe has a 30 s timeout, which kills the daemon mid-download; run_asr then falls back to run_asr_oneshot whose Command::output() has NO timeout — the one-shot re-starts the model download and blocks the transcribe worker thread indefinitely. During all of this state.busy stays true, the header pill shows 'Transcribing with local Whisper…', and every further dictation attempt is ignored (start_recording returns if busy). On stalled network this is a permanent, error-free soft-lock. Also: if the initial download exceeds the 900 s preload leash (slow Wi-Fi + 1.6 GB), the daemon is killed and preload is never retried this session.
findings.evidence: asr.rs:21-23 (TRANSCRIBE_TIMEOUT_SECS=30, PRELOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS=900), asr.rs:243-252 (timeout kills daemon), asr.rs:355-361 (fallback to one-shot), asr.rs:399-401 (cmd.output() with no timeout); asr_worker.py:148-149 (load_model — HF download happens here); lib.rs:1058-1065 (preload only if venv_py.exists() at launch), asr.rs:303-328 (preload_async, single attempt); lib.rs:337 (start_recording no-op while busy), lib.rs:229 ('Transcribing with local Whisper…' status)

findings.title: python_ok / status message lie on a fresh Mac: /usr/bin/python3 (CLT shim) satisfies exists(), so the app says 'Ready' and the 'ASR venv missing' branch is unreachable
findings.detail: resolve_python falls through venv → Homebrew paths → /usr/bin/python3, which exists as a stub binary on every macOS install even when Command Line Tools are absent. AppState.venv_python therefore points at an interpreter that cannot run the worker, yet build_status computes python_ok = venv_python.exists() = true and shows 'Ready — hold fn⌃ · double-tap hands-free'; the dedicated 'ASR venv missing — see Permissions' message can never trigger on a fresh Mac. The permission report's asr_probe does detect the problem ('lacks mlx-whisper. Click Install local ASR.') but that detail is only rendered in the main Permissions tab — the onboarding flow the fresh user is inside never shows it.
findings.evidence: asr_paths.rs:39-55 (fallback chain ending at /usr/bin/python3); lib.rs:232-233 ('ASR venv missing' branch gated on !venv_python.exists() — unreachable), lib.rs:244 (python_ok: state.venv_python.exists()); permissions.rs:104-122 (asr_probe correct detection); Onboarding.tsx:184-222 (permissions step renders ONLY Microphone + Accessibility — asrOk/asrDetail from the fetched PermissionReport are never displayed)

findings.title: Onboarding never tells the user ASR must be installed — the mandatory 'Install local ASR' step is buried in a tab they haven't seen yet
findings.detail: The first-run overlay walks welcome → permissions (mic + accessibility only) → calibration → done, and lets the user 'Finish setup' with allCriticalOk=false. The one action that could make the app functional on a fresh Mac (setup_asr_venv via the 'Install local ASR' button) exists only in the main window's Permissions tab, reachable after onboarding, flagged only by a 'Setup incomplete' banner that names Mic/Accessibility ('open Permissions to enable Mic / Accessibility') and never mentions ASR, Python, or a model download. Combined with the calibration hang (finding 2), the intended first-run path dead-ends before the user can ever discover the fix.
findings.evidence: Onboarding.tsx:10 + 31 (steps: welcome/permissions/calibration/done), Onboarding.tsx:191-212 (only two checklist items); App.tsx:774-779 (banner text mentions only Mic/Accessibility); App.tsx:798-810 (Install local ASR button, Permissions tab only); permissions.rs:149 (all_critical_ok = microphone && asr_ok)

findings.title: CLT-shim dialog storm: launch-time python probe + 1.2 s get_permissions poll each spawn /usr/bin/python3 on the main thread
findings.detail: On a CLT-less fresh Mac, every spawn of /usr/bin/python3 triggers macOS's 'would you like to install the command line developer tools?' flow. Yap spawns it (a) at launch before the window exists via python_has_mlx in run(), (b) ~600 ms later from preload_async (venv_py.exists() is true for the shim, so preload is NOT skipped — the daemon spawn + respawn-on-ping each exec the shim again), and (c) every 1200 ms while the user sits on the onboarding permissions step, because refreshPerms → get_permissions (a sync command on the main thread) → asr_probe → python_has_mlx execs `python3 -c "import mlx_whisper"` per poll. The user gets repeated system dialogs and main-thread jank during the exact screen asking them to grant permissions, with no explanation of why.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:1027 (python_has_mlx before UI), lib.rs:1058-1065 (preload gate is venv_py.exists() — true for the shim), asr.rs:304-327 (daemon spawn + second with_daemon ping); Onboarding.tsx:63-68 (setInterval refreshPerms 1200 ms), permissions.rs:113 + asr_paths.rs:133-139 (each report spawns python); lib.rs:748-750 (get_permissions is a sync command → main thread per lib.rs:871-877)

findings.title: Backend errors are surfaced only via macOS notifications, which a fresh Mac hasn't authorized
findings.detail: The dictation pipeline's error path reports failures with notify() (tauri-plugin-notification) plus last_error in the status event. On first run the app's notification permission is undetermined/denied until the user acts on the prompt, so the 'Yap — Failed: …' banner never appears; Onboarding ignores status events entirely, and the main window is hidden behind the onboarding overlay. Net effect: every fresh-Mac ASR failure is completely invisible, reinforcing the perception of an app that is simply 'loading forever'.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:302-309 (notify helper, result discarded), lib.rs:641-645 (Err path: notify + last_error only); Onboarding.tsx:83-97 (no 'status'/'paste_outcome' listener); tauri-plugin-notification usage lib.rs:34

findings.title: tauri.conf.json still pins the dev signing identity — locally-built DMGs given to another user are Gatekeeper-blocked (distinct failure from the loading hang)
findings.detail: bundle.macOS.signingIdentity is 'Apple Development: Wilson Guenther (U8BP8Z86T2)'. Any DMG produced by a plain `npm run tauri build` and handed to another Mac is unnotarized and dev-signed, so Gatekeeper refuses to open it ('Apple could not verify…'). The shipped v0.5.5 DMG was manually notarized with the Developer ID cert outside this config, so this is a footgun for every future build rather than the cause of the loading screen — but it must be ruled in/out when diagnosing another user's install (ask which DMG they got). Also note the binary is arm64-only (built on Apple Silicon, no universal target configured): on an Intel MacBook Air the app would not launch at all, and even after venv install `pip install mlx-whisper` hard-fails on Intel because MLX requires Apple Silicon.
findings.evidence: tauri.conf.json:53 (signingIdentity Apple Development); tauri.conf.json:38 (targets app/dmg, no universal target config); asr_paths.rs:119-124 (pip install mlx-whisper — Apple-Silicon-only package)

findings.title: Exact fresh-Mac first-run failure chain (chronological)
findings.detail: 1) Launch: run() seeds asr_worker.py to App Support and resolves python → /usr/bin/python3 CLT shim (asr_paths.rs:39-55); python_has_mlx execs it → first CLT dialog before any window (lib.rs:1027). 2) venv_py.exists() true → preload_async spawns the shim as a daemon → dies at EOF/15 s → warn in log only (lib.rs:1058, asr.rs:204-212). 3) Window opens; settings default onboarded=false → Onboarding overlay (App.tsx:680). 4) Permissions step: 1.2 s get_permissions poll re-execs the shim (dialog storm, main-thread jank); checklist shows only Mic/Accessibility — ASR-not-installed is computed (asr_ok=false) but never rendered. 5) Calibration: record → stop → busy=true 'Transcribing…'; pipeline: stop_and_transcribe → run_asr → daemon spawn fails → one-shot 'bad ASR JSON' → Err → log+notify only → no transcript event → busy stuck FOREVER = the infinite loading screen. 6) If the user escapes (Continue is still enabled) and finishes: status header claims 'Ready' (python_ok true); first dictation shows 'Transcribing with local Whisper…' then errors invisibly. 7) If they find Install local ASR: without CLT → instant vague toast failure; with CLT → main thread frozen for the entire pip download (no timeout). 8) After a successful install, the first dictation still hangs minutes+ in the untimed one-shot while the 1.6 GB model downloads under busy=true. Fix surface: bundle or auto-provision python+model (sidecar/externalBin + bundled small model), make setup_asr_venv/get_permissions async with progress events, clear Onboarding busy on a failure event, add a timeout to run_asr_oneshot, gate python_ok on python_has_mlx, and add an ASR-install step to onboarding.
findings.evidence: All file:line citations in findings 1-8; additionally Onboarding.tsx:259 (Continue enabled — disabled only by `recording`), lib.rs:1049-1055 (settings default), App.tsx:351-380 (refreshAll), asr.rs:143-222 (spawn_daemon ready-wait)

yap-latency.summary: Yap's warm-path latency (hotkey-release → paste) is dominated by: (1) non-streaming ASR — nothing is transcribed until key release, so decode time scales with clip length; (2) a per-utterance Silero VAD model rebuild — the tract ONNX model is loaded and re-optimized from disk on every dictation; (3) a serial post-stop DSP chain (high-pass, AGC, RNNoise at 48kHz, 16k resample, WAV write, WAV read-back, possible WAV rewrite) that only starts after release; and (4) fixed sleeps/polls (350ms blocking wait at record start, 50ms stop-flag poll, 30ms paste settle). On the press side, recording deliberately does not start until the 280ms hold-arm fires, plus cpal stream-open time — early speech is lost. Instrumentation exists for release→wav, release→asr-done, and total pipeline_ms, but there is zero timing for press→capture-start, DSP/Silero/RNNoise breakdown, python-side wav-load-vs-decode split, or paste dispatch.

findings.title: ASR is batch-only: transcription cannot begin until hotkey release (dominant, scales with clip length)
findings.detail: The whole pipeline is release-triggered: stop_and_transcribe spawns a worker that waits for the WAV to be finalized, then sends one 'transcribe' request for the full clip. Whisper decode time grows with utterance length, so a 20s dictation pays the full decode after release. The daemon+preload work (ModelHolder stays warm, greedy temperature=0.0, condition_on_previous_text=False) already minimizes per-request model cost, so the remaining decode time is architectural. Wispr-class latency requires streaming/chunked ASR during the hold.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:426-518 (stop_and_transcribe → record::stop_recording → asr::run_asr, all after release); asr_worker.py:156-198 (_transcribe_inprocess, single full-clip decode, temperature=0.0, condition_on_previous_text=False); lib.rs:122 default model mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo
findings.port_recipe: Chunked incremental decoding in the daemon: while recording, every ~3-5s ship the accumulated 16k buffer to the worker, transcribe the stable prefix (condition_on_previous_text off), and at release only decode the tail delta. Alternatively add a 'partial' cmd to asr_worker.py that keeps a rolling audio buffer per session. Even a two-phase scheme (decode first N seconds during hold, decode remainder at release) collapses perceived latency to tail-decode time.

findings.title: Silero VAD ONNX model is loaded + tract-optimized from disk on EVERY dictation
findings.detail: silero_probs() calls tract_onnx::onnx().model_for_path(...).into_optimized().into_runnable() inside the per-utterance path. tract graph load + optimization is typically 100-500ms — paid on every single dictation when denoise is enabled, before ASR can even be dispatched. The recurrent state is per-clip (correctly reset), but the compiled model itself is fully cacheable.
findings.evidence: record.rs:926-944 (model_for_path/into_optimized/into_runnable inside silero_probs, called from silero_isolate at record.rs:973-978, called per-stop at record.rs:143); gated by settings.denoise at lib.rs:474-479
findings.port_recipe: Cache the runnable model: static SILERO: OnceLock<Mutex<TypedRunnableModel>> keyed by model path/mtime; build it once in the existing startup background thread (where ensure_silero_model already runs) and have silero_probs borrow it. Only the Tensor state stays per-call.

findings.title: All clip DSP (high-pass, AGC, edge fade, RNNoise, 16k resample) runs serially AFTER release instead of during capture
findings.detail: record_loop accumulates raw f32 samples for the whole hold, and only after the stop flag fires does it run: downmix → high_pass → normalize_rms → edge_fade → optional denoise_rnnoise (which resamples the whole clip to 48kHz, runs a 10ms-frame NN over it, and resamples back) → resample_linear to 16k → write_wav_i16 to disk. Every stage is O(clip length) and sits between key-release and ASR dispatch. RNNoise plus two full-clip resamples is the largest chunk; for long dictations this is easily 50-300ms+ of pure serial post-processing.
findings.evidence: record.rs:439-477 (post-stop chain in record_loop), record.rs:659-719 (denoise_rnnoise with 48k round-trip resample), record.rs:481-496 (resample_linear), record.rs:476 (WAV write)
findings.port_recipe: Move the chain incremental: high_pass and RNNoise are both streaming-capable (biquad state, RNNoise frame state) — run them inside the cpal callback path (or a consumer thread fed by a ring buffer) so at release only normalize (needs global RMS — replace with running AGC), edge fade, and the final flush remain. Also resample once: capture→48k RNNoise→16k in one pass instead of native→48k→native→16k.

findings.title: start_recording blocks its caller for a fixed 350ms poll loop on the happy path
findings.detail: record::start_recording spawns the capture thread then loops `while !join.is_finished() && now < deadline(350ms) { sleep(20ms) }`. A healthy capture thread never finishes, so the caller ALWAYS eats the full 350ms. This runs inside lib.rs start_recording on the PTT event path, delaying the recording flag, the 'recording' emit, the floating pill, and system-output mute by 350ms after hold-arm. It also sets ActiveRecording.started AFTER the wait, so hold_wall_seconds under-reports by ~350ms, skewing the one latency stat that is persisted.
findings.evidence: record.rs:73-83 (deadline poll), record.rs:85-92 (started: Instant::now() after the loop); caller lib.rs:336-368
findings.port_recipe: Have record_loop signal success explicitly: an Arc<AtomicU8> or mpsc::channel set right after stream.play() succeeds (record.rs:429-431). start_recording waits on that signal (recv_timeout(350ms)) and returns the instant the stream is live; capture the `started` Instant at spawn time, not after the wait.

findings.title: Recording starts 280ms after key press by design (HOLD_ARM_MS) plus cpal stream-open time — leading speech is lost
findings.detail: The PTT state machine only fires PttEvent::Start after a 280ms hold-arm timer (to disambiguate tap vs hold), and capture only begins once cpal opens the default input device and stream.play() succeeds — device open on macOS commonly adds tens of ms (more on first TCC prompt or Bluetooth mics). Users who start talking as they press lose the first ~300-500ms of audio; Whisper then also mis-transcribes clipped onsets. This is press-side capture latency, not paste latency, but it is the biggest perceived-quality cost in the pipeline.
findings.evidence: ptt_macos.rs:30 (HOLD_ARM_MS=280) and ptt_macos.rs:355-376 (Start fired only after the arm sleep); record.rs:341-431 (device open + build_input_stream + play inside the spawned thread)
findings.port_recipe: Speculative capture: open the stream and start buffering immediately on combo-down; if the press resolves as a tap (< HOLD_ARM_MS), drop the buffer and stream. The stream open then overlaps the arm window instead of following it. Alternative/simpler: keep a persistent warm input stream (paused) so start is just 'begin appending', and/or drop HOLD_ARM_MS to ~150ms.

findings.title: Four disk round-trips of the same audio between release and ASR
findings.detail: The clip is (1) written as WAV by record_loop, (2) read back in stop_recording for energy VAD + Silero, (3) possibly REWRITTEN trimmed after Silero, then (4) re-read and re-decoded by the python worker from the path passed over stdin JSON. The in-memory f32 buffer that record_loop just produced is discarded and reconstructed from disk. Each hop is serial in the hot path; the WAV parse in python also re-does i16→f32 conversion (and a defensive resample path that should never fire).
findings.evidence: record.rs:476 (write), record.rs:127-136 (wav_duration_seconds + read_wav_mono_f32 read-back), record.rs:151-159 (trim rewrite via write_wav_i16), asr.rs:344-352 (path-only JSON request), asr_worker.py:82-131 (_load_wav_f32 re-decode)
findings.port_recipe: Return the 16k f32 buffer from record_loop alongside (or instead of) the file: pass samples through stop_recording so VAD/Silero/trim operate in memory, and write the WAV once, post-trim, only for the worker. Longer term: stream raw f32/i16 frames to the daemon over stdin (length-prefixed binary after the JSON header) and drop the file entirely.

findings.title: Stop-flag detection adds up to 50ms after key release
findings.detail: record_loop waits for stop with `while !stop.load() { sleep(50ms) }`, so key-release → capture-stop has a uniform 0-50ms quantization before any post-processing even begins.
findings.evidence: record.rs:433-435
findings.port_recipe: Replace with std::sync::Condvar or an mpsc channel notified from stop_recording, or drop the sleep to 5ms. Trivial ~25ms average win, zero risk.

findings.title: Paste path fixed costs: 30ms settle sleep + main-thread hop + three AX queries
findings.detail: After ASR: focus::should_auto_paste() does an AX focused-element query, copy_and_maybe_paste reads the prior clipboard, writes the transcript, re-samples the frontmost app via AX (YV21 guard), then dispatch_paste_on_main hops to the main thread (blocked if main thread is busy; 3s timeout) and sleeps a hard-coded 30ms before posting ⌘V. Typical total ~40-80ms — small vs ASR but pure fixed cost on every dictation. The 400ms clipboard-restore sleep is correctly off the critical path.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:562-564; paste.rs:66 (prior clipboard read), paste.rs:95-104 (AX frontmost re-check), paste.rs:135-145 (main-thread dispatch, 3s timeout), paste.rs:232 (sleep 30ms), paste.rs:112-119 (400ms restore, off-path); focus.rs:42-79 and focus.rs:82-102 (AX queries)
findings.port_recipe: Cut the settle sleep to 0-10ms (the notification/window focus-steal it defends against no longer happens before paste on this path — verify then reduce), read the prior clipboard concurrently with ASR, and log a paste_ms stage timer around dispatch_paste_on_main.

findings.title: Cold-path costs: daemon spawn/respawn, first decode, and 600ms preload delay
findings.detail: Warm daemon dies on ANY request error (with_daemon kills + respawns), and a respawn pays: python interpreter + mlx import + ready line (bounded 15s), then model map into ModelHolder (seconds for large-v3-turbo). preload_async deliberately sleeps 600ms at startup before warming, so a dictation in the first ~2-5s after launch is fully cold; the one-shot fallback (run_asr_oneshot) re-imports the entire stack per call. First-ever run additionally downloads weights (900s preload leash). Preload correctly warms both weights AND the mel/decode path with 0.1s of silence.
findings.evidence: asr.rs:262-300 (kill+respawn on any error), asr.rs:204 (15s ready wait), asr.rs:306 (600ms preload delay), asr.rs:355-361 (one-shot cold fallback), asr_worker.py:281-311 (do_preload with silence decode), asr.rs:21-23 (30s transcribe / 900s preload timeouts)
findings.port_recipe: Distinguish fatal vs transient errors in with_daemon so a single timeout doesn't discard a warm model; drop the 600ms preload delay to ~100ms (hotkey registration doesn't need 600ms); on respawn immediately fire a preload rather than waiting for the next dictation to pay the cold load.

findings.title: Timing instrumentation: good release-side totals, but press-side and per-stage breakdown are missing
findings.detail: EXISTS: t_release anchor with t_wav (release→wav ready), t_asr (release→ASR done), pipeline_ms (release→clipboard) logged and emitted as a 'latency' event; python reports per-request decode seconds and preload load_seconds; hold_wall_seconds captured; pipeline_ms + asr_seconds persisted per transcript. MISSING: (a) press→capture-start (the 280ms arm + stream open are invisible), (b) the 350ms start_recording block, (c) breakdown inside t_wav (stop-join vs DSP vs RNNoise vs WAV write vs energy-VAD vs Silero-load vs Silero-infer vs trim rewrite), (d) python split of wav-load vs model-check vs decode (only one 'seconds'), (e) IPC overhead (derivable as t_asr - t_wav - asr.seconds but never computed/logged), (f) paste/clipboard duration, (g) hold_wall_seconds is skewed ~350ms low by the start poll.

yap-tech.summary: Yap's core pipeline (record → warm ASR daemon → cleanup → paste) is well-hardened, but the distribution and first-run layers are not ready for a public any-machine install. The three critical structural gaps: (1) signing/updater config is dev-grade — an Apple Development signing identity is hardcoded, bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts is absent (Tauri 2 requires it), and the committed updater pubkey is a self-documented throwaway — so the shipped auto-update call can never work, yet it auto-installs with no opt-out when it someday does; (2) the ASR runtime is not bundled — it depends on the target machine having Homebrew/system Python 3 and does an unpinned `pip install mlx-whisper` at runtime via a synchronous Tauri command that blocks the entire main thread for minutes with no progress UI, and nothing gates on Apple Silicon; (3) several failure paths end in permanent spinners instead of errors — onboarding calibration soft-locks on any ASR failure, ASR preload failures are log-only so the UI says "Ready" while dictation is broken, and the one-shot ASR fallback has no timeout. Of the deferred punch list: dead commands show/hide_float_pill and recompute_stats are still present with zero frontend callers, the legacy JSON migration still ships (its dup-import sub-item appears already fixed), the updater still auto-installs with no opt-out, and CSP is still null.

findings.title: Hardcoded Apple Development signing identity — not distributable, and CI release signing will fail
findings.detail: tauri.conf.json pins signingIdentity to "Apple Development: Wilson Guenther (U8BP8Z86T2)". Apple Development certificates only validate on machines registered to the dev profile — Gatekeeper on any other Mac rejects the app (public install requires a Developer ID Application cert + notarization). Worse, the release workflow builds on a GitHub macos-14 runner that does not have this identity in its keychain and has no certificate-import step (no APPLE_CERTIFICATE/APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD secrets are used), so codesign with the configured identity fails on the runner. The APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY env passed to tauri-action cannot override the explicit tauri.conf.json value.

findings.title: Updater chain is broken end-to-end: no createUpdaterArtifacts, invalid v2 bundle target, throwaway pubkey
findings.detail: Three compounding problems: (a) tauri.conf.json bundle section has no createUpdaterArtifacts key — in Tauri 2 this is required for the bundler to emit the .app.tar.gz + .sig update artifacts (confirmed against v2.tauri.app/plugin/updater docs); without it no update artifacts exist for latest.json to reference. (b) release.yml passes `args: --bundles dmg updater` — "updater" is a Tauri v1 bundle target that no longer exists in v2. (c) The pubkey committed in tauri.conf.json is explicitly a placeholder: release.yml's own TODO says "the value committed there today is a THROWAWAY placeholder key" and a production keypair + TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret must be generated before the first real release. Net effect: the auto-update check that fires on every launch (main.tsx:13) can never find a valid signed update; it silently no-ops (swallowed in updater.ts catch), which masks the breakage.

findings.title: ASR runtime is not bundled — depends on host Python 3 + runtime unpinned pip install; no Apple Silicon gate
findings.detail: The MLX Whisper sidecar is created on the user's machine: resolve_python() hunts for /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.{13,12}, /usr/local/bin/python3, /usr/bin/python3 (asr_paths.rs:39-67), and setup_local_venv() runs `python3 -m venv` + `pip install -U pip mlx-whisper` with NO version pin (asr_paths.rs:98-124). Structural consequences for a public install: (1) a Mac without Homebrew Python or Xcode CLT has no usable python3 → the app installs fine but dictation can never work; (2) unpinned mlx-whisper means every new install gets whatever version pip resolves that day — the code even carries a TypeError fallback for older mlx_whisper APIs (asr_worker.py:191-194), evidence the API surface drifts; (3) mlx/mlx-whisper only run on Apple Silicon, but nothing checks the architecture — tauri.conf.json allows minimumSystemVersion 12.0 with no arch restriction, so Intel users get a broken install with no explanation. Onboarding never mentions ASR install at all (see separate finding), so the failure is discovered at first dictation.
findings.evidence: desktop/src-tauri/src/asr_paths.rs:39-67 (resolve_python candidates), :98-124 (setup_local_venv, unpinned pip install); desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:50 (minimumSystemVersion 12.0, no arch gate); python/asr_worker.py:191-194 (API-drift fallback)
findings.port_recipe: Either bundle a standalone python (python-build-standalone) + pinned wheels as a Tauri sidecar resource, or at minimum: pin mlx-whisper==<tested version>, detect arch via std::env::consts::ARCH and refuse/explain on x86_64, and surface the venv requirement in onboarding.

findings.title: setup_asr_venv and get_permissions are sync Tauri commands — minutes-long main-thread freeze during ASR install
findings.detail: In Tauri 2, non-async commands run on the main thread. setup_asr_venv (lib.rs:960-963) synchronously runs `python -m venv` + `pip install mlx-whisper` — a multi-minute network install — so the entire UI, tray, and event loop freeze while it runs; the only feedback is a toast fired BEFORE the invoke (App.tsx:799-806), no progress events. The codebase itself documents the sync-command-on-main hazard for paste_entry (lib.rs:871-877: "a *sync* command runs ON main and would deadlock") but doesn't apply the same treatment here. get_permissions (lib.rs:747-750, sync) also runs a python subprocess (`python -c 'import mlx_whisper'` via python_has_mlx, asr_paths.rs:133-139) plus a cpal device probe on the main thread — and Onboarding polls it every 1200 ms (Onboarding.tsx:66), causing recurring main-thread stalls during first-run.
findings.evidence: desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:960-963 (sync fn setup_asr_venv), :747-750 (sync get_permissions), :871-877 (own comment confirming sync commands run on main); desktop/src-tauri/src/asr_paths.rs:108-124; desktop/src/App.tsx:798-807; desktop/src/Onboarding.tsx:63-68
findings.port_recipe: Make both commands `async fn` + spawn_blocking (pattern already used by paste_entry at lib.rs:877), and emit progress events from setup_local_venv (pipe pip stdout lines to an "asr-install-progress" event).

findings.title: Onboarding calibration soft-locks on any ASR failure — permanent 'Transcribing…' spinner, error never shown
findings.detail: toggleCalibration sets busy=true when stopping a take (Onboarding.tsx:120-128); busy is ONLY reset by the "transcript" event listener (Onboarding.tsx:86-92). The backend emits "transcript" solely on pipeline success (lib.rs:603); on failure it sets last_error + sends an OS notification (lib.rs:641-645) and on the no-speech path it emits only "paste_outcome" (lib.rs:631-639) — Onboarding listens to neither "status" nor "paste_outcome". So on a fresh machine (no ASR venv — the exact population onboarding serves) or a silent take, the record button stays disabled showing "Transcribing…" forever (Onboarding.tsx:238-247). Onboarding's permissions step also only surfaces Microphone and Accessibility (Onboarding.tsx:191-212) — asrOk exists in the PermissionReport it fetches but is never rendered, so the one setup step a public user actually needs (Install local ASR) is invisible during first-run.
findings.evidence: desktop/src/Onboarding.tsx:86-92 (busy reset only in transcript listener), :120-128, :238-247, :191-212 (no ASR row); desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:603 (transcript only on Ok(Some)), :631-639 (Ok(None) → paste_outcome only), :641-645 (Err → notify + last_error only)
findings.port_recipe: Listen to "status" in Onboarding and reset busy when status.busy goes false, surfacing status.lastError; add an ASR row (asrOk/asrDetail + Install button) to the onboarding permissions step.

findings.title: First-run dictation failure modes: preload errors are log-only, 30s transcribe timeout kills mid-download, one-shot fallback has NO timeout
findings.detail: Three linked gaps in the sidecar lifecycle: (1) asr::preload_async failures (venv broken, model download failed, daemon won't start) are only log::warn'd (asr.rs:315-327) — no event, no status change, so the UI reports "Ready — hold fn⌃" while dictation is guaranteed to fail. (2) If the user dictates before the 900s preload finishes downloading whisper-large-v3-turbo (~1.6 GB), run_asr's transcribe request waits on the daemon mutex held by preload (with_daemon holds the slot lock across the request, asr.rs:262-300) — busy spinner for up to 15 minutes with the message "Transcribing with local Whisper…"; if instead the daemon is cold and the transcribe itself triggers the download, the 30s TRANSCRIBE_TIMEOUT (asr.rs:21) kills the daemon mid-download and falls back to (3) run_asr_oneshot, which uses cmd.output() with NO timeout at all (asr.rs:399-401) — it restarts the download and blocks the worker thread indefinitely; busy stays true (the WorkerBusyGuard at lib.rs:407-424 only fires on panic, not on an indefinite block), soft-locking dictation with a spinner. (3b) The daemon is also spawned with stderr → Stdio::null() (asr.rs:162), so the Python-side crash/traceback diagnostics that would explain failures are discarded.
findings.evidence: desktop/src-tauri/src/asr.rs:21 (30s), :162 (stderr null), :262-300 (mutex held across request), :315-327 (preload log-only), :399-401 (output() no timeout); desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:407-424, :228-229 (busy message)
findings.port_recipe: Emit an "asr-health" event from preload_async outcomes and fold it into AppStatus; use wait-with-timeout (e.g. wait_timeout crate or a killer thread) around the one-shot child; capture daemon stderr to the rotating log.

With no CSP, any script-injection foothold in the webview has full access to those IPC permissions. The float window also gets clipboard-read it never uses (over-grant).

findings.title: Settings persistence: corrupt file silently resets to defaults; non-atomic write; frontend last-writer-wins race
findings.detail: Startup load does `serde_json::from_str(&s).ok().unwrap_or_default()` — any parse error silently discards ALL user settings including onboarded (user gets re-onboarded and loses hotkey/model/tone config) with only default behavior as the symptom (lib.rs:1049-1055). save_settings writes with a bare std::fs::write — not write-to-temp-then-rename — so a crash/power-loss mid-write yields exactly the corrupt file the loader then silently discards (lib.rs:699-701). And the React layer sends the entire AppSettings object from its local copy on every save (App.tsx:511-519, saveSettings({...settings, ...})), so two writers (e.g. Settings panel and finishOnboarding, or a stale copy after the backend's profile→model remap at lib.rs:672-691) can clobber each other's fields — the backend even mutates the object (model, hotkey_label) after the frontend already optimistically setSettings(next) with the un-remapped copy.
findings.evidence: desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1049-1055 (silent .ok() load), :699-701 (fs::write), :672-697 (server-side remap); desktop/src/App.tsx:511-519 (optimistic setSettings(next) with pre-remap object)
findings.port_recipe: Write settings atomically (tmp + rename); log + rename a corrupt settings.json aside (like Database::open's quarantine) instead of silently defaulting; have save_settings return the canonical post-remap AppSettings and setSettings from the return value.

findings.title: Silero VAD model downloaded from a mutable branch URL with no checksum

No SHA-256 pin, so (a) upstream can change the file shape and silently break/alter VAD behavior across the install base, and (b) it's an unauthenticated remote artifact executed (inference) in-process. findings.title: tauri-nspanel pulled from a git branch (not a rev) — fragile reproducibility
findings.detail: Cargo.toml depends on tauri-nspanel via git branch "v2.1". Cargo.lock is committed so current builds are pinned, but any `cargo update` or lockfile regeneration (including by tooling/CI cache misses with --locked absent — the workflows run plain `cargo build`) resolves to whatever the branch head is that day. For a public release train this is the classic surprise-breakage vector.
findings.evidence: desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:44 (git = ..., branch = "v2.1"); .github/workflows/release.yml and ci.yml (cargo build without --locked)
findings.port_recipe: Change branch="v2.1" to rev="<current lock sha>" and add --locked to CI/release cargo invocations.

findings.title: Sidecar lifecycle otherwise sound (respawn/health/timeouts) — remaining gap is lazy death detection only
findings.detail: For balance: the warm-daemon design is solid — dedicated reader thread with recv_timeout so a hung worker can't block forever (asr.rs:177-201, 243-252), per-command timeouts, kill+respawn on any request error (asr.rs:288-299), dead-child detection via try_wait before each use (asr.rs:270-277), ready-line handshake with 15s bound (asr.rs:204-212), and Python-side EOF-driven shutdown so quitting Yap ends the daemon (asr_worker.py:346-398). The only lifecycle gap beyond the timeout findings above: daemon death is detected lazily at the next request rather than by any background health ping, so the first dictation after a daemon crash eats the respawn + model reload latency unannounced.

handy-engine.summary: Handy (v0.9.4) ships a fully-embedded, zero-sidecar ASR stack built on two engine crates: transcribe-cpp 0.1.3 (GGML/GGUF native inference — whisper, parakeet, canary, cohere, nemotron — with a compile-time Metal feature on macOS and streaming support) and transcribe-rs 0.3.8 with features=["onnx"] (legacy ONNX engines via ort 2.0.0-rc.12). Models come from a compiled-in JSON catalog (include_str! of catalog.json, generated from the handy-computer HF org) with pinned revisions, per-quant sha256 hashes, and a blob.handy.computer mirror; downloads go through a cjpais fork of hf-hub (branch cancellable-downloads) with a 4/1/1/1 retry ladder, 60s stall watchdog, resumable .partial files, mandatory sha256 verification, and mirror fallback, all reported to the UI via ~8 Tauri events. The TranscriptionManager keeps the loaded engine warm in an Arc<Mutex<Option<LoadedEngine>>> with an idle-unload watcher, catch_unwind panic containment, and an engine-lease system for live streaming preview. For Yap the minimal port is transcribe-cpp alone (skip transcribe-rs/ort entirely — Yap is Mac-only and the catalog's recommended models are all GGUF), plus the model manager/downloader/catalog trio, which kills the Python/MLX sidecar and adds live streaming transcription as a bonus.

findings.title: Engine crates: transcribe-cpp 0.1.3 (GGUF/Metal) + transcribe-rs 0.3.8 (ONNX-only) — NOT whisper-rs
findings.detail: Handy uses cjpais's own inference crates, both on crates.io. transcribe-cpp 0.1.3 (checksum 4c3c4d6...) handles ALL GGUF/GGML models — whisper family, parakeet-unified, nemotron, canary, cohere_asr, qwen3_asr, voxtral, etc. — with architecture auto-detected from the GGUF header; one EngineType::TranscribeCpp variant covers the whole family. Platform features: macOS = default-features=false, features=["metal"] (statically linked, init_backends_default is a no-op); Windows x86_64/Linux = ["dynamic-backends","vulkan"]; Windows ARM = static CPU-only. transcribe-rs 0.3.8 (features=["onnx"], pulls ort 2.0.0-rc.12) is retained only for legacy ONNX directory models: ParakeetModel, MoonshineModel/StreamingModel, SenseVoiceModel, GigaAMModel, CanaryModel, CohereModel. API surface used from transcribe-cpp: Model::load_with(path, &ModelOptions{backend, gpu_device}), model.session(), session.run(&audio_f32_16k, &RunOptions{task, language, target_language, family}), session.stream(&RunOptions, &StreamOptions::default()) for live preview, session.model().capabilities() (supports_streaming/translate/lang_detect/languages read from GGUF metadata), transcribe_cpp::init_logging(), init_backends_default(), devices(), backend_available(Backend). Supporting crates: hf-hub 0.5.0 (git cjpais/hf-hub branch cancellable-downloads, rev 9918f11, features=["tokio"]) for HF downloads with cancellation+progress; vad-rs (git cjpais/vad-rs rev 2a412ed, default-features=false, uses ort) for Silero VAD; reqwest 0.12 (json,stream) + futures-util + sha2 0.10 for the direct/mirror downloader; tar 0.4.44 + flate2 for legacy .tar.gz models; cpal 0.16 + rubato 0.16.2 for audio.

findings.detail: Three producers feed one HashMap<String, ModelInfo> registry inside ModelManager. (1) Bundled catalog: catalog.json is compiled into the binary via include_str! and parsed once into static CATALOG: Vec<ModelDescriptor>. Generated by scripts/gen_catalog.py from the handy-computer HF org; catalog_version 2; mirrors=["https://blob.handy.computer"]. Each entry: HF repo id (e.g. handy-computer/parakeet-unified-en-0.6b-gguf), pinned revision commit sha, languages, capabilities {streaming, translate, lang_detect, timestamps}, speed/accuracy scores (0-100, normalized to 0-1), files[] with per-quant {filename, quant, size_bytes, sha256}, default_quant, recommended flag + recommended_rank. Registry id = "{repo_id}/{filename-of-default-quant}". Recommended set (2026-07 catalog): rank1 Parakeet Unified EN 0.6B (streaming, Q8_0 default 731MB), rank2 Nemotron Streaming 3.5 (28 languages, streaming), rank3 Canary 180M Flash (218MB, tiny), rank4 Cohere Transcribe 2.0B (highest accuracy). (3) Discovery: discover_custom_transcribe_models scans the models dir for user-dropped .bin/.gguf (GGUF header probed for arch/capabilities via gguf_meta.rs; KNOWN_ARCHES gate), and discover_hf_cache_models scans the shared HF cache. rescan_local_models (Tauri command) re-runs both additively with a single-flight AtomicBool guard, then emits "models-updated". findings.title: Download flow: hf-hub with 4/1/1/1 retry ladder + 60s stall watchdog + resumable mirror fallback, sha256 as trust anchor
findings.detail: Entry: Tauri command download_model → ModelManager::download_model routes by ModelSource. HF path (download_hf_model): skip if hf_cached_path() or models_dir copy exists; register CancellationToken in cancel_flags map; RAII DownloadCleanup guard resets is_downloading on any exit. Retry schedule ATTEMPT_STREAMS=[4,1,1,1] — first attempt 4 concurrent range streams via ApiBuilder::from_env().with_token(None).with_progress(false).with_max_files(n), later attempts sequential (issue #1579: parallel streams all reset on some networks), exponential backoff 1<<attempt seconds between attempts. hf-hub has NO internal timeouts or retries, so a watchdog task polls progress every 5s and cancels a per-attempt child token when last_activity exceeds DOWNLOAD_STALL_TIMEOUT (60s); the whole download future is additionally raced against the token with a 5s grace so a wedge in the resolve/metadata phase can't hang forever. hf-hub commits a .sync.part resume offset so retries only re-fetch the remainder. After all attempts fail: mirror fallback via catalog::mirror_fallbacks — URL = {mirror}/{repo_id}/{revision}/{filename}; a mirror file is ONLY offered if the catalog carries its sha256 (mirrors are untrusted bit-pipes; the compiled-in hash is the trust anchor). Mirror + legacy-URL downloads share download_http_resumable: resumes from {filename}.partial with a Range header, defends against 416 (restart or hash-verify), 200-ignoring-Range (restart from zero), 206 with wrong Content-Range offset (discard), servers advertising/sending more than the catalog size (cut off + delete), verifies final size and sha256 (64KB-chunk hashing in spawn_blocking), then fs::rename .partial → final. Progress bridged via the hf_hub::Progress trait impl (HfDownloadProgress) and inline callbacks, throttled to 10 events/sec. UI events: model-download-progress {model_id, downloaded, total, percentage}, model-verification-started/-completed, model-extraction-started/-completed/-failed (legacy tar.gz only), model-download-complete, model-download-failed {model_id, error}, model-download-cancelled, models-updated, model-deleted. Frontend listens in src/stores/modelStore.ts (zustand) with typed tauri-specta bindings.

findings.title: Storage: shared HF cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub) + app-data models dir, pinned revisions with main fallback
findings.detail: Two storage locations. (1) Catalog/HF models land in the STOCK shared Hugging Face cache via hf_hub::Cache::from_env() — HF_HOME or ~/.cache/huggingface/hub — so models are shared with every other HF tool on the machine (a user who already pulled parakeet via python gets it for free, and vice versa). Lookup: Cache.repo(Repo::with_revision(repo_id, Model, revision)).get(filename), resolving through refs/<commit-sha> (pinned downloads) with a fallback to refs/main for caches populated before pinning or by other tools. (2) Everything else — legacy URL models, mirror-fallback downloads, extracted tar.gz directories, user-dropped custom .gguf/.bin — lives in {app_data_dir}/models (portable-mode aware via crate::portable::app_data_dir). get_model_path checks HF cache first, then models dir, and refuses to return a path while is_downloading or when a .partial/.extracting sibling exists (except a stale .partial next to a verified complete file, which it deletes). Deletion removes the snapshot pointer AND the blob it symlinks to in the HF cache. Directory models extract atomically: tar.gz → {name}.extracting temp dir → rename into place; interrupted extractions are cleaned up on next status scan. update_download_status recomputes is_downloaded/partial_size for every entry from disk, snapshotting in-flight download ids from cancel_flags first so a rescan can't clobber an active download's entry.

findings.title: Warm loading: engine held in Arc<Mutex<Option<LoadedEngine>>> with idle-unload watcher, take-out-then-return pattern, panic containment
findings.detail: TranscriptionManager owns the loaded engine. Load path (load_model_with_device): emits model-state-changed loading_started → get_model_path → drops the OLD engine BEFORE building the new one (avoids 2x peak RAM on large GGUFs) → Model::load_with(path, ModelOptions{backend, gpu_device}) → model.session() → reconcile runtime capabilities from session.model().capabilities() back into the registry → store Session in the mutex → emit loading_completed. The Session stays resident so repeated dictations skip reload. Keep-warm policy: a dedicated watcher thread wakes every 10s; if model_unload_timeout (settings enum ModelUnloadTimeout, includes an Immediately variant + timed variants) is exceeded since last_activity (AtomicU64 ms, touched on every transcribe/stream feed; kept fresh during recording), it unloads and emits 'unloaded'. Immediately-mode unloads right after each transcription via maybe_unload_immediately instead (never mid-recording). initiate_model_load spawns a background load thread when recording starts (single-flight via is_loading mutex + condvar; transcribe() blocks on the condvar until load completes). During transcription the engine is TAKEN OUT of the mutex (no lock held during compute) and the whole engine call runs under catch_unwind — a native panic drops the engine (auto-unload) instead of poisoning the mutex, clears current_model_id, and emits an error event; return_engine only puts it back if current_model_id still matches (a mid-flight model switch drops the stale engine). Streaming preview adds a lease system (active_engine_lease/active_stream_worker AtomicU64 worker ids + StreamWorkerGuard RAII) so the stream worker owns the engine while is_model_loaded() still reports true.

This replaces Yap's WarmDaemon (asr.rs) one-for-one: the Python daemon's preload/ping/kill-respawn machinery maps to initiate_model_load/is_model_loaded/the catch_unwind auto-unload. Yap's existing 30s TRANSCRIBE_TIMEOUT becomes unnecessary — in-process calls can't hang on a dead pipe, and panics are contained. findings.title: GPU/Metal: compile-time metal feature + load-time Backend selection, no runtime global for transcribe-cpp
findings.detail: macOS GPU is a Cargo feature (transcribe-cpp features=["metal"], statically linked), not a runtime flag. At startup, before any load, init_transcribe_backend() calls transcribe_cpp::init_logging() + init_backends_default() (no-op on static macOS builds; loads per-ISA CPU/Vulkan modules on dynamic builds) and logs the device registry from transcribe_cpp::devices(). Backend choice happens per model load: select_transcribe_backend maps the persisted TranscribeAcceleratorSetting {Auto, Cpu, Gpu} → Backend::{Auto, Cpu, Metal-on-macOS} (Gpu checks transcribe_cpp::backend_available(Backend::Metal) and falls back to Auto so a load never fails outright); resolve_gpu_device validates a stored multi-GPU registry index (irrelevant on Mac, 0 = auto). ModelOptions{backend, gpu_device} goes into Model::load_with; model.backend() reports what actually bound (e.g. CPU fallback under Auto). Changing the accelerator setting doesn't touch the live engine — reload_model_on_next_use marks it stale and the next use reloads. The separate ORT accelerator global (transcribe_rs::accel::set_ort_accelerator) only matters if transcribe-rs is included. GPU device list for UI: cached_gpu_devices from devices() filtered to non-cpu kinds, with VRAM totals.

findings.title: VAD: Silero v4 ONNX via vad-rs, 30ms/480-sample frames, threshold 0.3, SmoothedVad state machine (prefill 15 / hangover 15-55 / onset 2)
findings.detail: The VAD model silero_vad_v4.onnx is a build-time resource at src-tauri/resources/models/silero_vad_v4.onnx (fetched once from https://blob.handy.computer/silero_vad_v4.onnx per AGENTS.md; bundled via tauri.conf.json resources glob) and resolved at runtime via BaseDirectory::Resource. SileroVad wraps vad_rs::Vad (ort-backed) at 16kHz, frame = 30ms = 480 samples, speech iff prob > 0.3 (VAD_THRESHOLD); reset() clears the LSTM state between recordings. SmoothedVad wraps any VoiceActivityDetector with a debouncing state machine: buffers 15 prefill frames (450ms pre-roll emitted when speech triggers, so onsets aren't clipped), requires 2 consecutive voice frames to enter speech (onset), and keeps 15 frames (450ms) hangover for offline capture — reconfigured to 55 frames (1.65s) during streaming so the live decoder doesn't starve mid-pause (set_hangover_frames; one ONNX session serves both policies). Wired into AudioRecorder via .with_vad(...) in create_audio_recorder alongside a level callback (UI meters) and an audio-frame callback that feeds the StreamRouter for live streaming. preload_vad warms the ONNX session before the mic opens. Recordings shorter than 1s are zero-padded to 1.25s before transcription (audio.rs:762-764).

If Yap later wants Handy's exact stack, vad-rs pulls ort — avoid unless transcribe-rs is added anyway. Bundle silero_vad_v4.onnx as a Tauri resource instead of Yap's current runtime download.

findings.title: First-run model-download UX: onboarding gate + top-2 recommended cards + event-driven progress, auto-select only after onboarding
findings.detail: lib.rs checks at startup whether ANY model is_downloaded; if none, the main window is shown and the frontend renders Onboarding. Onboarding filters the registry to non-downloaded, non-legacy models (catalog arrives pre-sorted by recommended_rank), shows the first 2 recommended as ModelCards (Parakeet Unified + Nemotron Streaming in the current catalog) with the rest collapsed, and drives download → verification → extraction states purely from the events (downloadingModels/downloadProgress maps in modelStore). Selecting a model calls set_active_model → switch_active_model, which atomically claims the loading slot (try_start_loading guard), persists selected_model AND onboarding_completed=true BEFORE loading (so the UI reacts consistently to load events), skips eager loading if unload-timeout is Immediately, and reverts both settings if the load fails. Crucially, auto_select_model_if_needed refuses to auto-select while onboarding_completed is false — even if a compatible model already sits in the shared HF cache — so the user always makes the first choice explicitly; afterwards it clears stale selections (deleted models) and auto-picks the first downloaded model in ranked order. Model switching from the tray reuses the same switch_active_model path.

findings.title: Bonus port: live streaming transcription (transcribe-cpp Stream API) — real-time text in Yap's pill

handy-os.summary: Handy's OS-integration layer is substantially more hardened than Yap's on four fronts: (1) a dual-backend global-shortcut system (Carbon via tauri-plugin-global-shortcut + CGEventTap via the published handy-keys crate) with runtime switching, per-backend validation, a Secure-Input watchdog that shadow-registers shortcuts through Carbon when CGEventTaps go blind, and a serialized PTT/toggle coordinator with debounce + release-grace; (2) an audio pipeline that keeps a worker-thread cpal stream with device- and stream-config caches (saving ~80-200ms on the keypress→capture path), streams native-rate audio through a rubato resampler into 30ms 16kHz frames with inline Silero VAD, and drains to an EndOfStream sentinel so no tail audio is ever lost; (3) a receipt-sequenced "reliable paste" that publishes the transcript as a lazy NSPasteboard promise and restores the old clipboard only after the target app demonstrably reads it (vs Yap's fixed 400ms sleep, which is exactly the race Handy built this to fix); (4) an NSPanel overlay positioned on the cursor's monitor with a WebKit-leak guard and 30fps level throttling. Yap is ahead in two places Handy can't reach: the fn/fn⌃ CGEventTap gesture with hold/double-tap hands-free latch, and CoreAudio-native output mute/volume restore (Handy shells out to osascript). The must-ports for Yap are the receipt-sequenced paste, the device/config caching + preopened-stream capture path, the Secure Input fallback, and the coordinator-thread PTT state machine.

findings.title: Secure Input watchdog + Carbon shadow fallback — Yap's fn PTT dies silently without this
findings.detail: When any process holds Secure Event Input (password field, Terminal's Secure Keyboard Entry, stuck loginwindow), CGEventTaps stop receiving KeyDown/KeyUp while FlagsChanged still flows. Yap's fn⌃ tap is exactly this kind of tap: the fn part (FlagsChanged) keeps working but the interrupt-on-keydown logic and any keyed shortcuts die silently. Handy: a monitor thread polls Carbon's IsSecureEventInputEnabled() every 1s; after 3s sustained it (a) looks up the culprit PID by grepping ioreg for kCGSSessionSecureInputPID and resolves the name via ps -o comm=, (b) shadow-registers every vulnerable *keyed* binding through the Carbon-backed Tauri plugin (immune to secure input), widening side-specific modifiers (Carbon has no L/R distinction) and reporting covered/degraded/uncovered sets to the UI, (c) refuses the shortcut-recorder while secure input is active (otherwise the recorder captures only the modifier and destroys the binding — their issue #1578), and (d) dynamically shadows the Escape/cancel binding only while recording. Also ships a count-only keyboard diagnostic (tallies KeyDown/KeyUp/FlagsChanged/mouse without ever logging key identity) for user debugging.

findings.title: PTT/toggle coordinator thread: debounce + deferred-release grace, serialized lifecycle
findings.detail: All shortcut events for transcribe bindings funnel into one TranscriptionCoordinator thread (mpsc), which owns the Idle→Recording(binding)→Processing state machine. findings.title: Audio capture: persistent worker stream + device/config caches shave 80-200ms off keypress→capture
findings.detail: Handy's AudioRecorder opens a cpal stream on a worker thread that runs a consumer loop; recording start/stop are just Cmd messages, so in lazy/always-on modes the stream is already hot and capture begins with the in-flight buffer. Latency tricks, each measured in their debug logs: (1) named-device resolution cache — skips full cpal enumeration, ~40-110ms saved (audio.rs cached_device, keyed by name, invalidated on open failure so unplug self-heals via one retry); (2) SupportedStreamConfig cache per device name — skips two HAL property queries, ~40-85ms, worse on USB/BT (recorder.rs config_cache, cleared on failed open); (3) open() retry-once after cache invalidation before surfacing an error; (4) commands are processed BEFORE the in-flight audio chunk so Cmd::Start captures the buffer already in the channel — previously lost one buffer period (~10ms builtin, ~100ms BT) per start; (5) lazy_stream_close keeps the mic open 30s after stop (generation-counter cancellation, close serialized under the state lock so it can't close under an active recording); (6) records at the device's NATIVE rate and downsamples with rubato FftFixedIn to 16kHz 30ms frames — never forces hardware to 16k (breaks BT codecs/ALSA); (7) stop drains sample_rx until an EndOfStream sentinel the cpal callback emits after seeing the stop flag, with 2s timeout — guarantees every captured sample is consumed; (8) sub-1s clips zero-padded to 1.25s for Whisper; (9) VAD (Silero via vad-rs, SmoothedVad with prefill/onset/hangover frames, threshold 0.3) runs inline per 30ms frame during capture, reconfigured per session for offline vs streaming hangover; (10) format preference F32>I16>I32 at the native rate; (11) permission-denied and no-device errors classified from error strings and emitted as typed recording-error events for onboarding UX; (12) clamshell-mode mic override (ioreg probe, ~10-20ms, only when configured).

findings.title: Reliable paste: receipt-sequenced clipboard promise beats both Yap's 400ms sleep and Handy's own legacy path
findings.detail: Handy's paste_tx replaces 'write clipboard → send ⌘V → sleep → restore' (which loses the race whenever the target app reads late, pasting the user's OLD clipboard — their #502; Yap has this exact bug shape with a 400ms sleep) with an OS-notified handshake: (1) publish the transcript with declareTypes:owner: — a lazy PROMISE, no data on the pasteboard; (2) when any consumer reads, AppKit calls pasteboard:provideDataForType: on the owner — that callback IS the read receipt; (3) only receipts AFTER the ⌘V injection timestamp count (earlier reads are clipboard managers/AV reacting to the change); (4) restore after 200ms quiet-period past the LAST receipt (Chromium probes-then-reads multiple times), bounded by an 8s timeout, 500ms if chord injection failed; (5) restore only while changeCount is unchanged and no pasteboardChangedOwner: fired — a user copy always wins; (6) declares org.nspasteboard.TransientType/ConcealedType/AutoGeneratedType alongside so well-behaved clipboard managers (Maccy, Paste) skip the transcript — fewer eager readers makes receipts trustworthy, and requests for marker types don't count as receipts; (7) auto-submit Enter fires only after a confirmed receipt (never submits stale content); (8) a new paste settles the previous transaction first so its snapshot captures the real user clipboard; (9) failure mode is always 'transcript stays on clipboard a bit longer', never 'stale content pasted'. Publishing/injection on main thread (promises serviced by the main run loop), waiter on a worker, settle dispatched back to main. Chord itself: enigo with layout-independent virtual keycodes (Key::Other(9) for V on macOS) and a 100ms modifier hold, with a documented note that receipt detection makes a 10ms hold safely testable (~90ms latency win). Legacy fallback path also restores images (screenshot-clobber fix) and clears if the clipboard was empty. Pure evaluate() decision function is unit-tested.

findings.title: System-audio auto-mute: Handy's restore semantics are right, Yap's CoreAudio mechanism is better — merge them
findings.detail: Handy mutes system output while recording (mute_while_recording setting): on macOS it shells out to osascript 'set volume output muted true' and reads state back the same way. What's worth copying is the restore contract, not the mechanism: MuteState snapshots the PRIOR system mute state before muting; restore only unmutes if the system was NOT already muted (user's own mute is preserved); unknown prior state defaults to unmuting so audio is never stranded muted; did_mute guards against double-apply overwriting the snapshot with our own forced state; every stream open/stop path re-checks and restores. handy-app.summary: Handy (/Users/wilsonguenther/oss/handy) is a mature 18.4k-line Rust/Tauri 2 dictation app with production-grade settings resilience, a typed command bridge (tauri-specta), SQLite history with retention policies, a 7-platform signed/notarized release pipeline with post-bundle smoke audits, and zero analytics. Debug mode toggles via Cmd+Shift+D and a --debug CLI flag (runtime-only, not persisted). The keyboard diagnostic counts only event KINDS, never key identity. Yap's custom logging.rs (178 lines) covers file logging but has no runtime level control, rotation policy comment, or debug panel.
