wispr-changelog.summary: Wispr Flow's shipped surface (from wisprflow.ai/whats-new, /features, and docs.wisprflow.ai) breaks into five clusters: voice-driven editing (Command Mode, Transforms), text personalization (Snippets, auto-learning Dictionary, Styles), context awareness (reads text near the cursor via accessibility APIs, per-app/per-website category detection, on-screen name spelling), robustness (dictation recovery, retry, mic ranking/clamshell handling, 20-min sessions), and trust (secure-field exclusion, banking-app pause, local-retention options). Almost everything except cloud sync, teams/leaderboards, SSO, and the mobile apps is portable to a fully-local Mac app: their cloud LLM cleanup/rewrite passes map directly onto a small local model, and their context reading is plain macOS AX API work. The highest-leverage deltas for Yap are Command Mode, Snippets, a self-learning Dictionary, cursor-context awareness, backtrack correction, and dictation-audio recovery — all must-port. Yap already covers their core loop (PTT, local Whisper, paste, history, per-app modes, filler cleanup, analytics), so the gap is entirely in the intelligence and robustness layers, not capture.

findings.title: Command Mode — voice-driven edit/transform of selected text
findings.detail: Hold a secondary hotkey (Mac: Fn+Ctrl, customizable up to 4 bindings incl. mouse buttons), speak a command, release. With text selected (<1,000 words) Flow replaces the selection with the transformed result ('make this more assertive', 'translate to Polish', 'turn this outline into an essay'). Without selection it generates content or answers inline. Also supports meta-commands ('add a rule to never use exclamation marks' mutates cleanup settings) and a 'press enter' voice command that submits in chat apps. Gated behind paid plan; desktop only. Technically: capture selection, send selection+voice-command transcript to an LLM with an edit-instruction prompt, paste result over selection.
findings.evidence: https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4816967992-how-to-use-command-mode ; https://roadmap.wisprflow.ai/changelog/pray-command-mode-and-smarter-text-insertion-in-beta
findings.port_recipe: Second global hotkey in Yap's Tauri shortcut layer → grab selection via synthetic Cmd+C (save/restore NSPasteboard) or AXSelectedText → transcribe command with existing local Whisper → run local instruct model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct via llama.cpp/mlx, or Apple Foundation Models on macOS 26) with prompt {selection, command} → paste replacement via existing paste-to-frontmost path. 'Press enter' = detect the phrase in command transcript, post CGEvent for Return.

findings.title: Snippets — voice-triggered text expansion
findings.detail: User-defined trigger phrase (≤60 chars) → expansion text (≤4,000 chars); saying the trigger mid-sentence inserts the expansion in place ('my email signature', 'meeting link'). July 2026 added rich-text expansions (bold, italic, links, lists) preserved on paste. Technically it's post-STT phrase matching against the trigger table, substituted before insertion.
findings.evidence: https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/5784437944-create-and-use-snippets ; whats-new entry 2026-07-29 (v1.6.288) Snippets Rich Text Formatting
findings.port_recipe: Local JSON/SQLite snippet table + fuzzy match (normalized Levenshtein or embedding-free token match) over the final transcript before paste; replace matched span with expansion. Rich text: put both public.rtf/public.html and plain-text on NSPasteboard so rich targets get formatting and terminals get plain. UI: a table in Yap settings.

findings.title: Custom Dictionary with auto-learning, starring, and usage ranking
findings.detail: Manual add of proper nouns/jargon plus automatic learning from user corrections; March 2026 upgrade added starred (pinned) words, usage-based ranking of dictionary entries, and apostrophe filtering. Dictionary terms also feed capitalization preservation (proper nouns matching dictionary aren't lowercased mid-sentence). Technically: bias list injected into ASR decoding plus a post-correction pass, with a feedback loop that diffs what the user edits after paste.
findings.evidence: https://wisprflow.ai/features (Dictionary: 'learns corrections automatically'); whats-new 2026-03-31 (v1.4.661) Dictionary Upgrades; https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4678293671-feature-context-awareness (dictionary-driven capitalization)
findings.port_recipe: whisper.cpp initial_prompt biasing: prepend top-N ranked dictionary terms to the prompt (token budget ~224); plus deterministic post-pass regex/fuzzy replace for exact terms. Learning loop: after paste, watch the focused field via AX for ~10s and diff user edits against the transcript; promote repeated corrections into the dictionary with a confirmation toast. Store rank = usage count, starred = always in bias prompt.

findings.title: Context Awareness — reads text near cursor + app/website identity to steer formatting
findings.detail: Flow reads a limited amount of text around the cursor (before-cursor, selection, after-cursor), on-screen text, variable/file names in editors, and conversation history in Slack/Apple Messages; identifies the active app and, for browsers, the specific website (Gmail vs Docs). Uses it for: tone/format matching per app category, natural continuations (capitalize/punctuate correctly mid-sentence), proper-noun spelling from names visible on screen, skipping formatting when surrounding text is placeholder hint text (e.g. 'Reply to Claude…') or ≤2 words in Notion. Password fields are never read. Can be disabled in settings.
findings.evidence: https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4678293671-feature-context-awareness
findings.port_recipe: Pure AX API work, fully local: AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue on the focused element for kAXValueAttribute + kAXSelectedTextRangeAttribute to get before/after-cursor text; NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication for app identity; for browsers read AXDocument/AXURL from the focused window to key per-site modes. Feed {app, url, 500 chars of surrounding text} into Yap's cleanup-LLM prompt to decide capitalization of the first word, terminal punctuation, and proper-noun spelling. Skip entirely when AX role is AXSecureTextField.

findings.title: Backtrack / self-correction handling ('at 2… actually 3')
findings.detail: Mid-speech corrections are resolved so only the corrected version lands ('Let's meet at 2… actually 3' → 'Let's meet at 3'). This is an LLM cleanup-pass behavior layered on the raw transcript, adjacent to filler removal but semantically deeper.
findings.evidence: https://wisprflow.ai/features (Backtrack Correction)
findings.port_recipe: Extend Yap's existing filler-cleanup prompt/pass: add explicit instruction + few-shot examples for resolving 'actually/no wait/I mean/scratch that' corrections and dictated punctuation words. Cheap on a 3B local model; keep the raw transcript stored so the edit is undoable.

findings.title: Dictation recovery + failed-transcription retry
findings.detail: Audio is saved if the app quits mid-dictation and is recoverable/processable from History; failed transcriptions keep their audio for retry. (Their failure mode is server errors; a local app's are crashes and model-load failures — same UX applies.)
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-05-01 (v1.5.113) Dictation Recovery; Android 2026-03-31 Retry Failed Transcriptions
findings.port_recipe: Stream mic capture to a WAV in Application Support during recording (not RAM-only); on clean finish either delete or archive per retention setting; on next launch, scan for orphaned WAVs and offer 'Recover dictation' in Yap's history, running local Whisper on the file. Add a per-history-item 'Re-transcribe' button.

findings.title: Auto Cleanup levels (None/Light/Medium/High) with 'Undo AI edit'
findings.detail: Replaced a binary cleanup toggle with a 4-tier intensity control; original raw dictation is always preserved and one click reverts the AI edit. July 2026 postmortem noted an over-aggressive cleanup default hurt perceived accuracy — evidence that user-tunable intensity matters.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-04-24 (v1.5.55) Auto Cleanup Levels; 2026-07-09 Reliability & Accuracy Report
findings.port_recipe: Parameterize Yap's cleanup prompt by tier (None = raw Whisper; Light = fillers only; Medium = +punctuation/backtrack; High = +restructure/lists). Store {raw, cleaned} pairs in history; 'Undo AI edit' re-pastes raw. Per-app override slots into Yap's existing smart-mode table.

findings.title: Transforms — named rewrite presets with optional auto-apply after dictation
findings.detail: Built-in 'Polish' and 'Prompt Engineer' rewrite presets, run on-demand or auto-applied to every dictation; user-defined prompts can include personal writing samples so output matches the user's voice. Distinct from Command Mode: these are stored, reusable pipelines rather than ad-hoc spoken commands.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-05-01 (v1.5.113) Transforms Beta; https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2368263928-how-to-setup-flow-styles (writing examples fine-tune output)
findings.port_recipe: Preset store {name, system prompt, writing samples, auto_apply, per_app_scope} run through the same local LLM as cleanup. A 'Prompt Engineer' preset is high-value for Yap's Claude Code/Cursor audience: transform rambly speech into a structured agent prompt. Expose via pill menu and a hotkey.

findings.title: Styles — per-app-category formatting presets
findings.detail: Four app categories (Personal messaging, Work messaging, Email, Other) each get a formatting preset: Very Casual (no caps, light punctuation), Casual, Excited, Formal. Explicitly limited to capitalization/punctuation/spacing — never grammar or word choice. Applied automatically from detected app category. Yap's per-app smart modes partially cover this; the delta is user-configurable category presets and the lowercase/punctuation-density axis (the 'no caps in iMessage' behavior users love).
findings.evidence: https://wisprflow.ai/post/personalized-style ; https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2368263928-how-to-setup-flow-styles
findings.port_recipe: Add a category map (bundle-id/website → category) + per-category format preset in Yap settings; implement Very Casual/Casual/Excited/Formal as deterministic post-processing (lowercasing, terminal-period stripping, exclamation handling) so it's model-independent and instant, with the LLM pass only for Formal restructuring.

findings.title: Whisper Mode — reliable recognition of whispered speech
findings.detail: Marketed as: whisper quietly near the mic and it just works, no toggle. Whispered audio has no voicing/pitch, so naive VAD gates and low input gain are the usual failure points; large-v3-class Whisper models transcribe whispers decently once audio reaches the model at adequate level.
findings.evidence: https://wisprflow.ai/features (Whisper Mode)
findings.port_recipe: In Yap's capture path: apply AGC/gain normalization (or peak-normalize the buffer before inference), lower/disable energy-based VAD thresholds during PTT (PTT already bounds the segment, so VAD is optional), and test whispered samples against the shipped whisper.cpp model; if weak, offer large-v3-turbo as a quality tier. No cloud needed.

findings.title: Terminal-app paste handling (Claude Code / Codex)
findings.detail: Fixed long dictations 'collapsing into hidden text blocks' in Claude Code and Codex terminals — i.e., multi-line pastes triggering the TUI's bracketed-paste '[Pasted text #1]' collapse. They special-case insertion for terminal apps.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-05-01 (v1.5.113) Terminal App Support
findings.port_recipe: Detect terminal frontmost apps (Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, Warp, VS Code terminal focus) in Yap's per-app table; for them, either strip/join newlines before paste or use CGEvent keystroke injection instead of Cmd+V so the TUI treats it as typed input. Directly relevant since Yap's audience dictates into Claude Code.

findings.title: Microphone ranking, auto-selection, and clamshell mode
findings.detail: Users rank preferred mics once; Flow auto-switches to the highest-ranked available device on connect/disconnect. Clamshell support: switches to external mic when the lid closes, reverts on open, and warns when dictating on a closed MacBook with the built-in mic selected. Plus specific mic-error notifications (unplugged / in use / blocked by permissions).
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-06-24 (Automatic Microphone Selection, Clamshell Mode), 2026-05-01 (Microphone Error Clarity), 2026-03-31 (Clamshell Mode Warning)
findings.port_recipe: CoreAudio kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices listener for device add/remove; ordered preference list in settings; on change pick highest-ranked present device. Clamshell: detect via IOKit lid state or the built-in mic disappearing. Map AVAudioSession/CoreAudio error codes to specific pill/companion messages — fits Yap's cute-companion persona well.

findings.title: Customizable shortcuts: multi-binding, mouse-button PTT, Escape/Enter remap
findings.detail: Up to 4 shortcuts per action including non-primary mouse buttons for push-to-talk ('Mouse Flow'); rebindable Escape (cancel dictation) and Enter (send after paste); inline retry for dismissed transcripts.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-03-31 (v1.4.661) Mouse Flow + Customizable Shortcuts; Command Mode doc (4 shortcuts, mouse buttons)
findings.port_recipe: Extend Yap's hotkey layer with a CGEventTap listening for otherMouseDown/Up (buttons 3-5) as PTT triggers; add a keybinding UI supporting multiple bindings per action; optional 'press Enter after paste' per-app toggle (great for chat apps).

findings.title: Secure-field and sensitive-app protection
findings.detail: Password field contents are never read into context; Android auto-pauses in 50+ banking apps; context awareness can be disabled globally; local retention options (store normally / auto-delete after 24h / never store transcripts). Trust features that a local-first app can own even harder.
findings.evidence: https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4678293671-feature-context-awareness ; whats-new 2026-04-24 Local Storage Options; Android 2026-03-31 Banking App Privacy
findings.port_recipe: Before reading any AX context, check kAXRoleAttribute/subrole for AXSecureTextField and skip; per-app 'no history' blocklist (banking sites via browser URL match); history retention setting (keep / 24h TTL / off) — one cron-style sweep on launch. Cheap, and a marketing weapon: 'local model + never-store mode = nothing ever leaves the Mac'.

findings.title: Long dictations: 20-minute sessions with pre-limit warning
findings.detail: Session cap raised 5→20 minutes with a warning at 19; audio auto-saved at cap. For local Whisper this is a chunking problem, not a server-cost problem.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-03-31 (v1.4.661) 20-Minute Dictations
findings.port_recipe: If Yap holds audio in memory until PTT release, add rolling chunked inference: transcribe 30s windows with overlap (or VAD-split segments) during capture so release-to-paste latency stays flat regardless of length; show elapsed timer on the pill.

findings.title: Scratchpad — hotkey floating notepad for dictation
findings.detail: Option+S summons a floating rich-text notepad with tabs and version history (cloud-sync part excluded). Gives dictation a destination when no app field is appropriate.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-05-01 (v1.5.113) Scratchpad Beta
findings.port_recipe: Tauri always-on-top utility window with a local markdown store; 'dictate to scratchpad' when no writable AX field is focused (instead of failing the paste). Version history = append-only local snapshots.

findings.title: Language quick-switching in the overlay
findings.detail: One-click language picker in the Flow Bar for multilingual users; 100+ languages; routing fixes for dialects (UK English, Swiss German); regional dictionary prompt for Canadian English.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-03-31 (Language Picker in Flow Bar), 2026-06-17 (Language Routing), 2026-07-09 (Canadian English)
findings.port_recipe: Whisper is already multilingual: expose a language selector on Yap's pill (or auto-detect via whisper.cpp lang-detect on the first seconds) and pass the language token; per-language dictionary variants are a post-pass replace table.

findings.title: Insights 'Your Voice' profile
findings.detail: Beyond usage stats (which Yap has): a communication voice profile unlocked at 2,000 dictated words — characterizes the user's speaking/writing style. Pure retention/delight feature.
findings.evidence: whats-new 2026-04-24 (v1.5.55) Insights Tab
findings.port_recipe: Run the local LLM over accumulated history text to generate a periodic style card (top phrases, formality, avg sentence length); surface via the companion character — on-brand for Yap's Tamagotchi angle.

findings.title: Excluded as non-portable: cloud/team/platform features
findings.detail: Not portable or out of scope for local-only Yap: cloud sync + privacy-mode split, cross-device Scratchpad sync, team shared dictionary/snippets, leaderboards (Pro+Enterprise), batch invites/invite links, IT admin seats, HIPAA BAA, SSO/browser sign-in, status page, subscription sync, usage dashboards, desktop localization (portable but pure translation work), all iOS/Android keyboard items (switchback, Dynamic Island timer, smarter backspace, bubble UX), infra scaling/vendor redundancy entries. Their '30% latency reduction' is a cloud-inference metric; Yap's local pipeline competes on a different axis (no network RTT at all).
